data.name: Apt_HelpBody
data.value:
Assignment of IVAO airports to ACCs: here you decide each airport's owning ACC, from which the sector hierarchy and the public page follow.

  • Auto-assign creates the airports whose owning ACC is already in the DB and imports their sectors from the source.
  • Re-import all re-fetches runways and Transition Altitude for every assigned airport: many calls in a row, progress is shown in the header and can be stopped.
  • Group actions (move, generate documents, delete, assign) work on the ticked rows; whatever fails stays selected.
  • An airport with no sectors stays hidden from the public until it generates its documents.

The page shares the lock of the structure pages: one person at a time.

data.name: Ape_HelpBody
data.value:
The airport profile editor: every section opens and closes, and the dot next to its name means it has unsaved changes.

  • Save all (in the rail, also Ctrl+S) writes to the draft: the public sees it only after publishing, in «Versions».
  • Imported SIDs have their own save: edit the cells and press «Save changed».
  • Whatever comes from the source carries the lock and is not edited here: the policy lives in «Data sources».

data.name: Ape_RwRulesHelp
data.value: Each rule: when the indicated runways have tailwind ≤ the threshold, crosswind ≤ the threshold (optional) and the surface matches, they become preferential for departures/arrivals. Tailwind and crosswind are computed from the current wind. They are evaluated in order: the first that applies wins (put the more specific ones on top). If none applies, the runway with the best headwind is used.

data.name: Xfer_HelpBody
data.value: An agreement binds two lists of units for one kind of traffic, over every airport listed; the clauses say which points it applies to and at what level. Both directions are always visible, and «us/them» depends on the ACC you opened — not on how the agreement was written. The Gaps button tells you where to work. In the operational view, if a unit is closed the hierarchy is climbed up to the first online one (otherwise UNICOM).
